steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our EasyPortrait dataset paper (face parsing and portrait segmentation for video conferencing). Explain the app requirements that motivated it, what the data needs to look like, and our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Video conferencing apps and their features
- Our goal and app requirements
- Requirements for the model and the data
- Contributions: EasyPortrait dataset and collection pipeline
- What the experiments check

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Video conferencing apps
  - popular in corporations (online meetings) and habitual life (relatives far away)
  - features: face beautification, background blur, noise reduction
  - improve user experience: change background, smooth skin
- Our goal
  - integrate these features into video conferencing app
  - real-time CPU-based on user's device, highly accurate
  - robust to amount of context, backgrounds, persons in frame, poses, attributes (race, age), accessories (headphones, hats)
  - nice to have: teeth whitening, accurate background change with transparent glasses lenses and uneven hair
- Model and data requirements
  - deep learning models for portrait segmentation and face parsing
  - real-time, no delays, fine-grained masks
  - data: 1) heterogeneous (subjects, head turns, subject-to-camera distance, scenes, accessories like eyeglasses, headphones); 2) main face parsing classes ("skin", "brows", "eyes", "lips") + extra "teeth"; 3) accurate annotation for both tasks at once -> one model, save resources
- Contributions
  - existing datasets unsuitable (Sec. 2) -> EasyPortrait dataset
  - pipeline with two crowdsourcing platforms: Yandex.Toloka, ABC Elementary
  - 40,000 image/mask pairs, 13,705 individuals; domain-suitable scenes, head poses, accessories
  - ethnic diversity: users from various countries and continents
  - manual annotation, 9 classes, specially designed rules
- Experiments
  - number of samples and head-pose diversity help robustness and effectiveness (Sec. 4)
  - generalization: cross-dataset evaluation (Sec. 5)

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Video conferencing apps became popular quickly, in corporations for online meetings and in everyday life to keep in touch with relatives who are far away. Because of this, these apps got many useful features, such as face beautification, background blur, and noise reduction. These extensions can make the user experience better, letting users change the background or smooth their skin.

Our work mainly aimed to add these features to the video conferencing app. The app has to give a real-time CPU-based experience on the user's device and give a very accurate response. Also, our system has to be robust to the amount of context in images, the backgrounds, the persons in the frame, their poses, their attributes (e.g. race and age), and accessories (headphones, hats, etc.). It is also better to improve the user experience with functions like teeth whitening and accurate background changing when there are transparent glasses lenses and uneven hair.

These requirements put restrictions on the solution and on the training dataset. We decided to use deep learning models that solve portrait segmentation and face parsing tasks. The system has to work in real-time without delays and give fine-grained segmentation masks. The data we need has to be 1) heterogeneous in subjects, head turns, subject-to-camera distances, scenes, and the accessories that are specific to videoconferencing, like eyeglasses and headphones; 2) annotated with the main face parsing classes ("skin", "brows", "eyes", and "lips") and also an extra class "teeth"; 3) accurately annotated for both tasks at the same time. The last point means only one model can be trained for all the use cases, which saves limited resources for model inference.

- Contributions
  - existing datasets do not fit (Sec. 2) -> EasyPortrait dataset
  - collection + labeling pipeline on Yandex.Toloka and ABC Elementary
  - 40,000 pairs of images and masks from 13,705 people; suitable scenes, head poses, accessories
  - ethnic diversity, users from many countries and continents
  - 9 classes annotated manually with specially designed rules
- Experiments: sample count and head-pose diversity help (Sec. 4); cross-dataset evaluation for generalization (Sec. 5)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Video conferencing apps became popular quickly, in corporations for online meetings and in everyday life to keep in touch with relatives who are far away. Because of this, these apps got many useful features, such as face beautification, background blur, and noise reduction. These extensions can make the user experience better, letting users change the background or smooth their skin.

Our work mainly aimed to add these features to the video conferencing app. The app has to give a real-time CPU-based experience on the user's device and give a very accurate response. Also, our system has to be robust to the amount of context in images, the backgrounds, the persons in the frame, their poses, their attributes (e.g. race and age), and accessories (headphones, hats, etc.). It is also better to improve the user experience with functions like teeth whitening and accurate background changing when there are transparent glasses lenses and uneven hair.

These requirements put restrictions on the solution and on the training dataset. We decided to use deep learning models that solve portrait segmentation and face parsing tasks. The system has to work in real-time without delays and give fine-grained segmentation masks. The data we need has to be 1) heterogeneous in subjects, head turns, subject-to-camera distances, scenes, and the accessories that are specific to videoconferencing, like eyeglasses and headphones; 2) annotated with the main face parsing classes ("skin", "brows", "eyes", and "lips") and also an extra class "teeth"; 3) accurately annotated for both tasks at the same time. The last point means only one model can be trained for all the use cases, which saves limited resources for model inference.

Existing datasets do not fit our production purposes because of the limitations in Sec. 2. This is why we created the EasyPortrait dataset, which is our first contribution. The second one is a pipeline for collecting and labeling images with fine-grained segmentation masks using two crowdsourcing platforms, Yandex.Toloka and ABC Elementary. With it we collected 40,000 pairs of images and segmentation masks from 13,705 individuals in domain-suitable scenes, with different head poses and various accessories specific to videoconferencing apps. We thought ethnic diversity was important for problems based on persons and their facial attributes, so we collected images from users from various countries and continents. The images were annotated manually with 9 classes following specially designed rules, so all the cases described above are covered.

We checked that data characteristics like the number of samples and their diversity in head poses have a positive effect on how robust and effective the model is (Sec. 4). We also assessed how well the training data generalizes with cross-dataset evaluation experiments (Sec. 5).

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Video conferencing apps have quickly gained popularity, both in corporations for online meetings [1] and in our everyday life to keep in touch with relatives from a distance [2]. As a result, these apps have been enhanced with various beneficial features, including face beautification, background blur, and noise reduction [3]. Such extensions can improve the user experience, allowing users to change the background or smooth their skin [4].

Our work primarily aimed to integrate these features into a video conferencing app. The app should ensure a real-time CPU-based experience on the user's device and produce highly accurate results. Besides, our system needs to be robust to the amount of context in images, backgrounds, persons in the frame, their poses, attributes (e.g. race and age), and accessories (headphones, hats, etc.). Finally, it is preferable to improve the users' experience with functions such as teeth whitening and accurate background changing in the case of transparent glasses lenses and uneven hair.

All these requirements impose restrictions on the solution and the training dataset. We decided to use deep learning models solving portrait segmentation and face parsing tasks. The system must function in real-time without delays and produce fine-grained segmentation masks. The suitable data must be 1) heterogeneous in subjects, their head turns, subject-to-camera distances, scenes, and videoconferencing-specific accessories like eyeglasses and headphones; 2) annotated with the main face parsing classes ("skin", "brows", "eyes", and "lips") and an extra class "teeth"; 3) accurately annotated for both tasks simultaneously. The last allows training only one model for all possible use cases and saves limited resources for model inference.

Existing datasets are unsuitable for our production purposes due to the limitations described in Sec. 2. This motivated us to create the EasyPortrait dataset, our first contribution. The second is a pipeline for gathering and labeling images with fine-grained segmentation masks using two crowdsourcing platforms, Yandex.Toloka and ABC Elementary. It allowed us to collect 40,000 pairs of images and segmentation masks from 13,705 individuals in domain-suitable scenes with different head poses and various videoconferencing-specific accessories. Considering the importance of ethnic diversity for problems based on persons and their facial attributes, we collected images from users in various countries and continents. Images were annotated manually with 9 classes according to specially designed rules, which allowed us to cover all the described cases.

We verified that data characteristics such as the number of samples and their diversity in head poses have a positive impact on the model's robustness and effectiveness (Sec. 4). The generalization ability of the training data was also assessed through cross-dataset evaluation experiments (Sec. 5).

[2] How video tech can bring us closer than ever. https://inlnk.ru/Vo8ydV (2023)
